title: Convex session fallback orchestrator for edge active-active
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Background:
Redwood's hosted API must keep user-facing sessions (including streaming chat) healthy during cross-region perturbations. Current active-active routing drains by region-level weight flips which causes abrupt stream interruptions for long-lived sessions. We need a coordinated orchestration layer at the edge that: (1) shifts traffic with convex weighting to avoid oscillation, (2) preserves stream continuity where possible, (3) exposes circuit-breaker metrics to SLO logic, and (4) performs graceful load shedding for lower-priority work to protect P99 latency for paid tiers.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Session continuity: For in-flight streaming sessions, attempts should be made to preserve KV cache and token continuity within SLA constraints. If continuity is impossible, provide a graceful short-resume response so client can resume without repeating the entire conversation.
- SLO adherence: During regional flaps, system maintains 99th percentile token latency within configured SLO bands for paid customers (contracted SLO) and degrades best-effort for free or low-tier traffic.
- Minimal user-visible truncation: Less than 1% of paid streaming sessions should be terminated unexpectedly during a region failover in 95% of failover experiments.
- Circuit breakers: Adaptive circuit breaker engages per-region and per-model variant when error-rate or queue-latency windows exceed thresholds; fallback routing executed to alternate variants or regions.
- Observability: New metrics and dashboards for convex-weight transitions, per-session continuity outcome, circuit-breaker state, and shedding counts.

Design summary:
1) Convex weight ramping: Replace linear weight shifts with convex ramp (fast initial move + taper) to reduce oscillation when health feedback is noisy. Configurable curve per route and per-customer.

2) Stream-aware soft-drain proxy (edge orchestration):
   - When a region is de-prioritized, mark new connections to cold region as REJECT_FOR_SHARDING but keep existing streaming connections open for a maximum grace window (configurable, default 60s) unless underlying model instance signals state loss.
   - Maintain lightweight session tokens that capture minimal continuity metadata (epoch, last-kv-checkpoint, watermark) that can be used by destination replicas to attempt a fast rehydrate.
   - If rehydrate fails, return a standardized short-resume envelope with last-ok-turn id + suggested resume prompt.

3) Circuit-breaker & load-shed policy:
   - Two-tier circuit breaker: tenant-level and region-level.
   - Error-rate window uses EWMA with tunable alpha to detect spikes faster while smoothing noise. Thresholds linked to SLO budgets; breaker will first attempt fallback to compatible model variant in same region, then to alternate region depending on routing policy.
   - Load shedding: token-budget-aware shedding that prunes non-essential background requests (embeddings for analytics, low-priority batch reranks) while preserving interactive generation. Shedding decisions are tagged and emitted to telemetry for chargeback and RCA.

4) SLO-aware routing engine:
   - Incorporate per-tenant SLO priorities into routing decisions. For tenants with strict P99 targets and Reserved Dedicated customers, traffic should be favored and provided longer rehydrate attempts.

5) Observability & Tracing:
   - New tracing span t.edge.failover.transition, metrics: edge.transition.curve, session.continuity.outcome{success,recovered,fallback,terminated}, breaker.state{closed,open,half-open}, shed.count, shed.reason, rehydrate.latency.
   - Dashboards: Per-region failover heatmap, per-tenant continuity rate, SLO burn-rate correlated to transitions.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (prototype): implement convex weight curve and simulate in canary with traffic mirror. Add unit tests for ramp shapes and hysteresis. (ENG dev branch + RFC PR #3012)
- Phase 2 (edge soft-drain): implement soft-drain proxy changes, session-token envelope, and rehydrate APIs. Expose a feature flag per region. Add integration tests with streaming harness.
- Phase 3 (breaker + shedding): ship adaptive breakers with EWMA windows and token-budget shedding filters.
- Phase 4 (canary & rollout): deploy in us-west-2 as canary 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% across non-critical routes; monitor session continuity, P99 latency, error-rate, and shed counts.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests: weight ramp math, token envelope serialization, breaker state machine.
- Integration: simulate regional outage at gateway level and assert continuity outcomes vs baseline.
- Load tests: synthetic streaming sessions (10k concurrent) across two regions with induced latency spikes to verify shedding preserves paid-tier P99.
- Chaos experiments: orchestrate partial control plane disruption and measure edge behavior.

Runbook snippets (for SRE):
- If edge.transition.curve shows repeated oscillation: rollback to linear weight curve and open ticket to investigate health feedback noise (common causes: bad healthcheck, GC spikes).
- If session.continuity.outcome shows elevated 'terminated' for paid tenants: temporarily increase soft-drain grace window and enable cross-region rehydrate / degraded-fastpath.
- If breaker.state is OPEN but error-rate is low in backend: check for metric skew or EWMA alpha misconfiguration.

Rollout & metrics gates:
- Gate 1 (canary 5%): session continuity >= 98% for paid test tenants, no increase in paid P99 beyond 5% relative.
- Gate 2 (25%): circuit-breaker false-positive rate <1% (closed->open flips per hour normalized).
- Gate 3 (full): sustained SLO compliance for 72h and manual sign-off from SRE and PM.

Artifacts & links:
- RFC proto & design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Convex+Edge+Failover+RFC
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-orch/pull/3012
- Streaming test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-harness/tree/convex-drain
- Canary dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/edge/convex-failover-canary

Open questions / trade-offs:
- State sync cost vs truncation risk: attempting aggressive rehydrate (full KV snapshot) improves continuity but increases network and latency risk. We will start with metadata-only fast rehydrate and measure.
- Curve tuning: convex vs sigmoid vs exponential — need empirical tuning across real traffic shapes.
- Client compatibility: do we require SDK changes to interpret short-resume envelope? We'll add backward-compatible fallbacks and keep plain-text resume suggestions in response body.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Schedule PM/OSS work to update SDKs with resume handling for mobile/web clients.
- Perf microbench on kernel selection when rehydrate path is used under high concurrency.
- Add automated e2e chaos job to CI that runs weekly to validate continuity contracts.

Acceptance tests (automated):
- continuity_contract.spec: assert fewer than 1% paid-session terminations under simulated cross-region failover at scale 1k sessions for 5 minutes.
- breaker_false_positive.spec: assert breaker flip rate <1% under synthetic healthy but delayed backends.
